name: Civil Engineering
overview: The first years build a base in calculus, physics, mechanics, chemistry and geology, then move into surveying, CAD and BIM, hydraulics, soil mechanics and strength of materials. Core civil subjects follow: construction materials, structural analysis, steel and reinforced concrete structures and foundation engineering, with business law, economics and urban development alongside. A surveying field course gives hands-on practice, and the degree ends with a bachelor thesis. You choose between Structural Engineering (high-rise buildings, halls, frames) and Infrastructure Engineering (roads, railways, water utilities, environmental engineering). Graduates work on bridges, tunnels, power stations, industrial plants and multi-storey buildings.

name: Computer Science Engineering
overview: The first four semesters share a common foundation of calculus, probability, statistics, algorithms and the theory of computing, together with electronics and physics. Professional subjects then cover digital engineering, computer architecture, communication networks, operating systems, programming in C, C++ and Java, databases, software engineering, computer graphics, artificial intelligence and IT security. From semester five you specialise in either Software Engineering or Infocommunication. An eight-week internship and a thesis project complete the degree. Graduates move into a master's programme or into designing, building and running software and data systems.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: You start with mathematics, physics and electronic materials, then move into core electrical engineering: microelectronics, electronics, instrumentation, control systems and programming, drawing on both classical and modern methods. The course aims at a balance between theory and practical engineering work. Three specialisations are offered: Embedded and Control Systems, Infocommunication, and Sustainable Electric Energetics. A six-week internship and a thesis project round off the seven semesters. Graduates are prepared for engineering roles in electrical and information technology fields.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The programme begins with mathematics (vector algebra, calculus, differential equations) and engineering basics such as physics, technical drawing and machine elements, plus professional English. Later subjects include design and manufacturing, electronics and control, fluids and heat transfer, and materials science, taught with laboratory and design work. You then specialise in Process Engineering (energy processes, fluid systems, CFD, waste management) or Design and Technology (CAD, injection moulding, composites, manufacturing systems). An individual project, an internship and a thesis conclude the degree. Graduates become design engineers, project managers and consultants in automotive, aerospace, energy and manufacturing.

name: Vehicle Engineering
overview: The degree opens with mathematics and physics (linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, statics and dynamics), then adds the basics of mobility, project work and economics. From there you specialise in one transport area: automotive, vehicle mechatronics, rail vehicles, aircraft, vessels or manufacturing. A thesis project closes the seven semesters. The training covers design, production, testing, maintenance, repair and recycling of transport equipment and vehicle systems. Graduates take up junior engineering tasks in the vehicle industry or continue to a vehicle engineering master's.

name: Engineering Management
overview: Engineering and business are taught side by side: mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry and mechanics on one side, business economics, psychology, accounting, statistics and quality management on the other, with materials, transport science, civil engineering and production management in between. The course is strongly project-based, with a project module, a six-week internship and a thesis. In the later semesters you pick a track in Management, Sustainability and Environmental Management, Product Management or Financial Management. Graduates work in quality, service, production, project or environmental management and consulting, or continue to a master's.

name: Professional Pilot
overview: Aviation is studied on an engineering base of mathematics, physics, programming, electronics, thermodynamics and fluid dynamics. Aeronautical subjects include the principles of flight, airframes and systems, powerplants, human performance and control systems, followed by navigation, meteorology, flight planning and operations. Flight training runs alongside the theory, ending with multi-crew cooperation training in an Airbus A320 environment, and a thesis is part of the degree. Graduates can hold a commercial pilot licence with a multi-engine instrument rating and go on to first officer or cadet positions with airlines in countries where EASA certificates apply.

name: Physics
overview: You begin with experimental physics (mechanics, electricity, thermodynamics, modern physics), mathematics, programming and electronics, with a lot of time in laboratory exercises. Later you take theoretical mechanics, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, statistical physics, optics and solid-state physics. In the final year you choose between a Physicist specialisation, which leans towards theory and programming, and an Applied Physics one, with more lab work and informatics. The thesis involves research with international teams in areas such as quantum physics, nanotechnology, materials, medical physics and data science. Graduates go into research or industries like semiconductors, optics, medical devices, nuclear energy and data analysis.

name: Physicist-Engineer
overview: This course pairs engineering with a stronger natural-science base than most engineering degrees: mechanics, electrodynamics, optics, thermodynamics, condensed matter and statistical physics, together with advanced mathematics. You also learn programming, numerical algorithms and machine learning, plus measurement methods, CAD, electronics and sensing. Specialisations cover nanotechnology and quantum applications, nuclear technologies and sustainable energetics, or scientific data processing. It was developed with industrial partners and includes a six-week internship and a thesis. Graduates move into research and development, data science, AI, energy, medical devices and semiconductors, or on to engineering or physics master's programmes and PhDs.

name: Mathematics
overview: The first year covers calculus, algebra, geometry and combinatorics, before the course branches into analysis (including differential equations and functional analysis), algebra, differential geometry, discrete mathematics, probability, statistics and operations research. Programming and mathematical modelling run alongside, with accounting and economics courses as a practical side. You choose elective advanced topics, such as numerical methods, stochastics or a research project, and finish with a bachelor thesis. Graduates work in banking, investment, insurance, consulting, data mining and telecommunications, or continue to a master's in mathematics or applied mathematics, and to a PhD.

name: Chemical Engineering
overview: You build a base in mathematics, physics, general, physical and biochemistry, then move into inorganic and organic chemistry, chemical engineering, chemical technology, environmental technology, analytical chemistry, unit operations and process control. The course combines theory with modern laboratory work, a six-week internship and a thesis. From the fifth semester you choose between chemical and process engineering, industrial pharmaceutics, or materials science. Graduates work in industrial technology, research and development, planning and public administration, or continue to the master's in chemical engineering.

name: Architectural Engineering (single-cycle)
overview: One continuous degree leads straight to a master's-level qualification, mixing creative and technical training. You practise freehand drawing, visualisation and modelling, work in design studios on housing, public buildings, workplaces and urban design, and study mathematics, statics, structures, building construction, building services, CAAD and BIM, along with architectural history and heritage preservation. From the fourth year you can specialise in Real Estate Development, Sustainable Architecture or Urban Design. A diploma design project and a practice placement finish the course. Graduates enter architectural practice or continue to doctoral study.

name: Culture, Politics and Society
overview: The first year lays foundations in cultural anthropology, sociological theory and political concepts and ideologies, drawing on history, philosophy, international relations, law, public policy, gender studies and environmental studies. In year two you choose one of three multidisciplinary majors, learn research methods and complete an experiential project such as an internship, work with a faculty researcher or civic engagement. Minors in areas such as gender studies, human rights or philosophy are possible, a year at a partner university is an option, and thesis seminars lead to a final thesis. Graduates go into public policy, international organisations, NGOs, media, cultural industries and research, or on to a master's.

name: Data Science and Society
overview: The first two years combine calculus, linear algebra and statistics with Python programming, algorithms, machine learning, data management and the ethics of AI, plus microeconomics and quantitative methods. In years three and four you follow one of three tracks: Economics, Politics and Policy, or Social Cognitive Science. Classes rely on discussion and collaboration, with data science projects on real-world data from business or academia, an option to study at a partner university in year three, and thesis research. Graduates head for startups, fintech, government bodies, research institutions and policy consultancies, or for master's study in data science, economics, politics or finance.

name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics
overview: Year one covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, politics, political concepts, philosophy of knowledge and ethics, along with academic writing, critical reasoning and data analysis. In year two you pick two of three pairings: Economics and Politics, Philosophy and Economics, or Politics and Philosophy, with electives from other programmes. Small seminars stress discussion; the third year offers exchange at a partner university or an experiential project such as an internship or civic work, and the later years centre on a thesis, with master's-level courses possible in year four. Graduates work in public administration, non-profits, media and advocacy, or continue to master's study in fields like international relations or finance.

name: Applied Economics
overview: The first year covers introductory economics, empirical methods, calculus, linear algebra and probability, plus business basics and a project. Year two moves to macro and microeconomic theory, accounting, international economics, two econometrics courses, game theory and AI in business. In year three you study corporate finance, public economics, industrial organisation and the history of economic thought while preparing a thesis. Mathematics is taught as a practical tool, and individual and group assignments build presentation skills. Many students go on to a master's; graduates also work as macroeconomic, market or financial analysts and actuaries in companies, banks, insurers and consultancies.

name: Business and Management
overview: Year one builds on data analysis, statistics, micro and macroeconomics, accounting and organisational management; year two turns to marketing, corporate finance, managerial accounting, business law, strategy, operations, HR and project management. In year three you choose from 27 specialisations, such as AI-driven management, corporate finance, digital business, entrepreneurship or sustainability management. Teaching uses case studies, group projects and business case competitions, and the final year is a long internship plus thesis. Double-degree routes exist with Kedge Business School in France and EBS in Germany. Graduates work in finance, marketing, HR, project management, controlling, logistics and analytics.

name: Business Informatics
overview: The first year mixes calculus, linear algebra, probability, economics, programming and an introduction to data science and IT architecture. Year two adds databases, software engineering, AI applications, finance, law, IT project management and business process management. Year three covers intelligent systems, machine learning, ERP systems, business analytics, cybersecurity and digitalisation projects. The course is practice-oriented, with projects done with real companies, case study competitions and a mandatory internship from the fifth semester, followed by a thesis. Graduates work as business systems developers, designers, business intelligence specialists, analysts and IT managers in large firms, financial institutions and startups.

name: Communication and Media Science
overview: The first year pairs communication with philosophy, economics, international politics, quantitative social research and persuasive and visual communication. Year two adds qualitative methods, media literacy, language in culture and society, data visualisation and digital marketing communication. Year three brings project and campaign communication, a compulsory internship and a thesis seminar. Teaching is project-oriented, with media studio work. You choose one of five specialisations: Public Communication, Business Communication, Global Connections and Communications, Community Communication or Global Social Challenges. Graduates work as media specialists, PR experts and social media managers.

name: Data Science in Business
overview: The first two years build mathematical and statistical foundations (calculus, linear algebra, probability) using Excel and R, with Python and SQL programming taught from scratch, plus economics, accounting, databases, data visualisation and statistical modelling. Later years turn to machine learning, business intelligence and project courses such as data-driven business decisions, worked on corporate datasets in the university's data labs. A long internship and a thesis complete the degree. Exchange places are available through the university's partner network. Graduates work as data analysts, BI consultants, AI specialists and financial analysts.

name: International Relations
overview: Year one covers philosophy, global history, economics, introductory international relations and social research methods, with training in persuasion and academic writing. Year two adds world economics, post-1945 history, international law and the geopolitics of the USA, UK, Europe and international organisations. Year three covers security studies, global political economy, China, Russia, the Middle East, India and Latin America, with a thesis seminar and a compulsory internship. Teaching uses simulations and case projects, and you choose from six specialisations including European Studies, World Economy and Hungarian Political System. Graduates go into diplomacy, international organisations, NGOs and the international departments of companies.

name: International Business
overview: The first year covers business essentials, mathematics, micro and macroeconomics, accounting and data analysis; year two adds law, corporate finance, marketing, cross-cultural management and project-based problem solving. Year three turns to international trade practice, negotiation and European business, and a full semester abroad, studying or interning, is part of the course. Teaching is problem-based, with case studies and teamwork in small groups, ending with an internship and thesis. You can concentrate on Global Markets and Marketing, Global Economy and Business, Entrepreneurship, or International Supply Chain Management. Graduates work as trade experts, logistics and sales managers, analysts and consultants, or found their own firms.

name: Philosophy, Politics, Economy (PPE)
overview: The first year introduces all three disciplines: logic and moral and political philosophy, comparative politics and political decision-making, and economics, together with research methods and themes such as sustainability and AI. Year two links them through the individual, community and society, advanced political economy and global governance. Year three is for specialised study and two thesis projects. After year two you pick one of eight specialisations, such as Economics and Philosophy, Modern Political Problems or Global Social Challenges, and study abroad is recommended in year three. Graduates work as policy analysts, economic analysts and government relations specialists.

name: Psychology
overview: The course is built on four core subfields: cognitive and affective psychology (memory, perception, emotion), personality, developmental and social psychology, supported by biological psychology, research methods, statistics and ethics. Electives touch clinical, health, educational and organisational applications. Research field practicals in each subfield feed into the BA thesis, which gathers empirical work from those placements and is defended in the final exam. Small classes give a tutorial-like atmosphere. Graduates qualify as behaviour analysts supporting psychologists in educational, clinical, organisational and rehabilitation settings, work as HR or research assistants, or continue to a psychology master's.

name: English and American Studies
overview: After the first term you pick an English or an American track. The English track covers English literature, British and American political culture, academic writing and spoken argument, and the linguistics of phonology and syntax. The American track concentrates on American history, culture and literature and the American variety of English, with an emphasis on critical thinking and research. Teaching is by lectures and seminars, and the degree does not give a teaching qualification. Graduates can continue to a master's in English or American studies or work in journalism, tourism, government bodies, diplomacy or private-school English teaching.

name: Computer Science
overview: Mathematics and theoretical computer science sit at the centre, applied through programming languages and compilers, software technology, algorithms, data science and engineering, information systems, numerical analysis and computer algebra. Areas such as artificial intelligence, robotics, cryptography and cybersecurity are part of the picture. Teaching takes place in computer labs for AI, databases and robotics, with large team projects, peer mentoring from senior and PhD students, and optional undergraduate research under faculty supervision. Graduates work as programmers, software engineers and web developers in IT companies, banks, research institutes and universities.

name: Applied Economics
overview: The course gives general economics training with a social, political and international slant: economic concepts, principles and theories, rigorous methodology, and an introduction to other social sciences and business studies. It looks at how individuals, firms and nations make strategic choices and at the political and social forces behind them, using deductive reasoning and mathematical models. The broad, general design is meant to keep career choices open. Graduates work as business, financial and market analysts or in marketing and sales, in government, NGOs, media and sport, or continue to a master's in economics, business, sociology or international relations.

name: International Relations
overview: You study international politics, security, EU politics, ethnic conflict, global justice and human rights, on a base of sociology, law and economics. The first year is made up of introductory courses, after which a wide range of elective seminars lets you shape your own path. Graduates work as foreign policy analysts, lobbyists, project coordinators or political advisers in public administration, NGOs, financial and commercial institutions and private firms, or they continue to a master's in international relations or another social science.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: Studied at the Savaria University Center in Szombathely, the course covers applied solid and fluid mechanics, computer-aided design and engineering, and finite element analysis, with production and manufacturing technology including Industry 4.0. Theory is paired with work in laboratories for materials science, production technology and control, which hold tensile testers, CNC machines and electron microscopes, and in computer labs running Ansys, Solid Edge, Inventor, ADAMS and Matlab. Graduates become design, production, automation or simulation engineers in manufacturing, vehicle production and research.

name: Kindergarten Education
overview: The course combines psychology, pedagogy, methodology and language skills, with child development, differentiated lesson planning and activities for children aged three to six. Play-based education, a distinctive feature of Hungarian kindergartens, is central. The programme is practice-oriented, with a series of placements throughout the studies, and the faculty runs a Play Lab and workshops for educators. Graduates work as kindergarten or day-care teachers in municipal, church-run and private settings.

name: International Business Economics
overview: Year one covers management, marketing, accounting, mathematics, economics and business law basics, with an introduction to AI applications. Year two adds corporate finance, business statistics, international finance and economics, international political economy, taxation and marketing research, together with argumentation and persuasion. Later years bring leadership, international financial management, EU law and economics and negotiation, plus electives such as data analysis with Python and business ethics. Project work, one or two semesters of compulsory internship and a thesis make it practice-oriented. Graduates work as business development managers, economic analysts, consultants and trade specialists in international firms.

name: Sociology
overview: The programme trains professional sociologists in sociological concepts and research methods, and in recognising and interpreting social problems. Lectures and seminars are combined with project-based teaching, including a semester of intensive project work. You can add a specialisation such as data analysis or criminology, which carries an extra certificate. Graduates work in research, public administration, media, social and health services, marketing, HR and management, in roles such as community officer, social worker or marketing analyst, and can continue in social sciences at other European universities.

name: Finance and Accounting
overview: The first two semesters cover management, marketing, accounting, mathematics, business law and economics. The next two bring corporate finance, controlling, international finance, taxation and business statistics, and later semesters turn to investment financing, international financial management and a two-semester project. The final semester combines a thesis with a compulsory internship. Electives include business law, social sciences and data analysis with Python. The degree gives exemptions from some ACCA exams. Graduates work as controllers, financial analysts, accountants, auditors, tax advisors and finance managers in multinational companies.

name: Early Childhood Education
overview: The course prepares you to work with children from birth to three in nurseries, combining pedagogical competence and early-years methodology with a strong emphasis on practical training. You can follow a specialisation in Innovation in Early Childhood Education or in German Nationality Early Childhood Education, and a double-degree option with the University of Florence lets a few students spend their second year abroad. Graduates work as nursery educators in public and private institutions or as self-employed childcare providers.

name: Special Needs Education
overview: The first semesters give a general introduction to special needs education and its related fields, including human biology, theory of education, psychology and the arts. From the third semester you specialise in one or two of four areas: hearing impairment, intellectual disability, visual impairment, or physical and multiple disabilities. Field visits run through the course, and the last semester is a professional practice period in an institution linked to your specialisation. Graduates work as early intervention specialists, special school teachers, inclusive education support teachers and rehabilitation instructors in education, healthcare and social services.

name: Pedagogy
overview: You study the education system, modern learning theories, research methods, psychology, history, philosophy and sociology of education, educational policy and digital education. Equal opportunities (inclusion, child protection, educational rights) and self-awareness and skills training are part of the core. The first four semesters give foundations and the last two focus on the Digital Education specialisation, covering educational technology and online learning management. Internships and projects take place in a range of educational institutions. Graduates work as educational developers, e-curriculum developers, digital educational assistants, project assistants and programme coordinators.

name: Chemistry
overview: A research-oriented degree built on a strong foundation in mathematics, physics and the core chemical disciplines, giving you a theoretical understanding from the molecular to the macroscopic scale. Much of the learning is hands-on: extensive laboratory work, modern chemical instrumentation, data analysis and an introduction to academic research practice. Graduates can continue to a master's and PhD in chemistry or take entry-level jobs in chemical laboratories, analytical and quality control and research and development, including in materials science, environmental analysis, biotechnology and pharmaceuticals.

name: Animation
overview: You follow a production from idea and script through storyboard and animatic to animation and post-production, studying story development, storyboard drawing, animation film language, drawing animation, puppet animation, 3D modelling and motion, 2D digital animation, sound design and compositing. Teaching is hands-on, with professional software and instructors from the industry. From the third semester you specialise in Creative Animation, which blends digital and classical techniques, or in 3D Animation, with spatial modelling and effects. Graduates work in animation studios, film production, game development, graphic design and advertising, or freelance.

name: Environmental Design
overview: The course explores how people relate to the built environment through interior and object design, sustainable and health-conscious solutions, CAD and 3D modelling, drawing, painting, form studies and design and art history. Year one introduces forms, spaces and materials through practical foundation work; year two focuses on interiors, furniture and architecture; year three centres on one large complex design project. Teaching relies on personal consultation, practical workshops with in-house prototyping and real-life internship placements. The specialisation is Interior and Spatial Design. Graduates work as interior designers, object designers, design consultants or independent artists.

name: Film and Media Studies
overview: The first year covers film history, writing, directing, camera, lighting, editing and sound, with photography, documentary and short fiction projects. In year two you work on fiction scenes and feature films with actor direction, studio and multi-camera work, and short films from scripts developed in dramaturgy classes. Year three is concentrated practical work in writing, directing, editing, sound, music and producing, including preparing pitches for international platforms. Theory in film history, visual analysis and production management runs alongside. You find your role in directing, cinematography, editing, sound or producing, with internships at production companies, festivals and post-production firms.

name: Graphic Design
overview: The first year builds manual and digital skills through illustrations, covers, logos, pictograms and image identities. Year two covers book and magazine design, typography, packaging, branding, corporate identity and sustainable design, and year three turns to complex integrated projects, interactive and web graphics, mobile apps, UI and UX design and a diploma project. Teaching rests on individual consultations and project work on realistic briefs, supported by print workshops (screen printing, lithography, linocut, risography), laser cutters, 3D printers and bookbinding. You can specialise in Graphic Design or Packaging Design. Graduates work as freelance designers, art directors, illustrators and web or UI designers.

name: Media Design
overview: The course trains media creators who shape technology with artistic sensitivity, across screen graphics, motion pictures, sound design, 3D, game design and UX design. Year one builds creative potential, visual logic and composition; year two deepens 2D and 3D design and interactive applications; year three is made up of complex projects carried out with industry professionals. You choose between two tracks: Multimedia, covering UX and web design, visual effects, sound design and projection mapping, or Game Design, covering visual, level and character design, storytelling and sound. Graduates work in post-production studios and game companies, or as independent media artists.

name: Communication and Media Studies
overview: You study communication theory, advertising and media planning, digital marketing, and public relations theory and practice, together with social studies and psychology. Creative communication courses, social projects and media projects supply the practical side. From the third semester you choose International Communication, with cross-cultural skills, international relations and two working foreign languages, or Integrated Media, which teaches print, radio, television, online and social media together through project-based learning. Graduates work as journalists, editors, press officers and spokespeople, in PR and marketing management, event organisation and international affairs.

name: International Relations
overview: The first semesters give broad introductions to the social sciences and the history of international relations, followed by core subjects such as diplomacy, international organisations, international law and modern international history, plus political science, economics, law and research methods. The course stresses communication, negotiation and writing. You choose between Diplomacy and International Communication, with security and foreign policy analysis and model diplomacy exercises, and International Development Cooperation, with a semester-long project. The final semester brings a thesis and a compulsory internship. Graduates become diplomats, policy analysts, NGO and think tank staff or public administrators, or continue to a master's.

name: Human Resource Management
overview: The first three semesters give a business foundation, built on the idea that an HR specialist is a business expert focused on people, work processes and organisational culture. You then study the main HR functions: recruitment and selection, training and development, compensation, competency management, employer branding, labour law, industrial relations, organisational behaviour, leadership and performance management. Elective tracks are HR Branding, HR Technology and Digitalization, and HR Training and Development, and the final semester is practical experience in a company. Graduates work in multinationals, HR consultancies, recruitment and employer branding agencies, tech startups and the public sector.

name: International Business Economics
overview: The course covers EU integration and EU policies, globalisation and world economic regions, foreign trade strategy and international competitiveness, logistics, marketing fundamentals, management, international economics, international trade and finance, and negotiation techniques. It is designed to give knowledge that transfers across many positions in domestic and international business, and in civil and economic diplomacy. Graduates can work in business or in communication and social science fields, or continue to business programmes.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: You study accounting, business law, micro and macroeconomics, finance, human resources, management and organisation, marketing, statistics and strategic planning, with business informatics, controlling, logistics, project management and international economics. Teaching uses case studies of industry practice and a simulated business environment, and a partnership with the Young Entrepreneurs Association Hungary offers networking. You can add a specialisation in Financial Management, Global Marketing or International Business. Graduates become enterprise managers, business communicators, environmental managers, EU economic relations experts and start-up managers.

name: Commerce and Marketing
overview: The first semesters cover the economic, social and technological environment and marketing fundamentals, followed by integrated marketing communications, market research, e-business, advertising and media planning, public relations, branding, digital and content marketing. Learning is project-based, with case studies and tasks set by leading companies under the guidance of industry experts. In the later semesters you specialise in Advertising and PR or Global Marketing, and the last semester combines a thesis and an internship. Graduates work as marketing experts in companies and agencies, start-up or SME managers and non-profit specialists.

name: Finance and Accounting
overview: You start with finance, corporate finance, accounting, calculus, statistics and business economics, then move to taxation, investments, financial law, strategic planning, audit, risk and control, insurance, project financing and management accounting. Specialised modules include accounting for financial institutions, controlling, accounting information systems, international financial accounting for multinationals, IT support for finance and consolidated annual reporting. Working with current software is emphasised, and you choose a Finance or an International Accounting specialisation. Graduates work in banking, securities, insurance, consulting and audit firms, corporate finance, tax advice and government finance.

name: Tourism and Catering
overview: Year one covers economics, marketing, statistics, law, tourism geography and leisure marketing. Year two introduces hotel management, catering and gastronomy, attractions and destination management and health tourism, and year three adds travel agency management, international negotiation, languages and a personal portfolio project. Teaching is project-based, with professional competitions, workshops, hotel visits, seminars at cooperating hotels. You specialise in Health Tourism (thermal baths, medical spas, wellness) or International Hotel Management, with work placements through partners such as Accor, Danubius and Mellow Mood. Graduates become hotel and spa managers, tour operators, tourism consultants and event organisers.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: The degree is practice-oriented, mixing mathematics, statistics, economics and market research with finance, accounting, marketing, management, HR and project management, and later topics such as supply chain management, strategic planning, controlling, innovation, crisis management and digital marketing. A semester-long compulsory internship, a project module and a thesis defended in the final exam tie it to practice, and optional cooperative training modules with partner companies are available. You choose a specialisation in Project Management and B2B Marketing or in Digital Manager. It prepares you to organise and manage enterprise activities and to continue to a master's.

name: Commerce and Marketing
overview: The programme combines economics and business methodology with social sciences and core commerce and marketing subjects; final exams include trade economics, foreign trade techniques, marketing management and marketing communication. In the later semesters you choose between Digital Marketing Communication and Project Management and B2B Marketing. A compulsory professional internship of at least twelve weeks in the last semester and a thesis defended in the final exam complete the degree. Graduates are economic professionals for the supply and sale of products and services, including managing the commercial side of small and medium enterprises, and can go on to a master's.

name: Computer Science Engineering
overview: You study advanced programming and software technology, database design, big data and business intelligence, operating systems and networks, server services and security, mobile app development, embedded systems and robot programming, cloud computing and information security. From semester four the specialisation is Cloud Service Technologies and IT Security: IT infrastructure, virtualisation, distributed systems, containers, IoT, big data and DevOps. Electives reach into bioinformatics, robotics and intelligent systems, the thesis can be done with company support, and Erasmus exchange with partner universities is possible. Graduates enter the job market or continue to a master's.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: The degree rests on natural science fundamentals, economics and humanities and a large block of professional electrical engineering knowledge, taught through lectures, seminars and compulsory laboratory practice, with project work, reports and presentations. In the final semesters you follow Applied Electrical Engineering, a broad specialisation joining building automation, infocommunication networks, sensors and actuators, artificial intelligence, energy systems, solar power and data transmission, aimed at flexibility across automation, energy, renewables and industrial systems. A six-week traineeship and a thesis complete the programme, which leads on to master's study in electrical engineering.

name: Engineering Management
overview: You study mathematics, physics, electrotechnics, chemistry and materials science alongside enterprise economics, HR management, accounting, law and marketing, with a professional core of technical drawing, manufacturing technology, quality, innovation and project management, decision support systems, lean management and logistics. Later you choose a track as Project Manager, in Process Management or in Corporate Management. A mandatory six-week internship with an outside organisation, project work and a defended thesis are included, and a voluntary cooperative training module lets you work on site with partner companies.

name: Environmental Engineering
overview: The course draws on biology, chemistry, physics, ecology and earth sciences, and on environmental protection topics: water, air and soil quality, noise and radiation protection, and waste management. Technology subjects include wastewater treatment, renewable energy systems, environmental simulation and GIS, with environmental law, quality management and project management alongside. Learning involves laboratory work, field measurements, a project course, a required internship and a thesis. You can follow Sustainable Energy Management and Green Energy, or Sustainable Land Development and Water Management. Graduates work as environmental managers in enterprises and plants, or continue to the university's Environmental Engineering master's.

name: Industrial Design Engineering
overview: Design and engineering are taught together: freehand drawing, form design, modelling, design visualisation, colour theory and art studies on one side, and mathematics, physics, technical mechanics, machine elements, CAD/CAM and technical documentation on the other, with enterprise economics, marketing, project management and environmental studies. Studio and lab work counts toward grades. You choose between Product Design, centred on interior, textile and fashion accessories with sustainable approaches, and Packaging Design, covering packaging materials, printing technologies and eco-friendly design. An internship and a thesis are part of the degree, which prepares for a master's.

name: Mechatronical Engineering
overview: Mechanical engineering is combined with electronics, electrotechnics and computer control, resting on mathematics, mechanics, electricity and informatics applied at systems level. The course suits people who like to experiment and see their ideas working in practice. You can specialise in Robotics or in Intelligent Control Systems. Graduates are prepared to design and build smart devices and robots with artificial intelligence, or to continue to a master's degree.

name: General Medicine
overview: The six-year medical degree runs in three stages. A basic module covers the structure and function of the healthy body through anatomy, histology, embryology and biochemistry; a preclinical module turns to pathology, microbiology and patient examination skills; and the clinical module teaches specific diseases and their diagnosis and treatment, mostly in the hospital wards. Direct experience with patients at the bedside or in the operating theatre is central, and the final year is a full practical year in the wards, where students carry out medical work under supervision. Clinical areas include cardiology, paediatrics, neurology, psychiatry, surgery, obstetrics and oncology.

name: Dentistry
overview: The first two years cover physics, chemistry, biochemistry, cell biology, anatomy, histology, general and oral microbiology, pathology and behavioural sciences. A preclinical stage follows, with internal medicine, surgery, dental pre-clinics, diagnostic imaging and pharmacology, and then intensive clinical study of each discipline of dentistry, including preventive dentistry, oral surgery, restorative dentistry with implants, paediatric dentistry and orthodontics. The aim is to unify basic and clinical sciences so that theory and practice develop together, with hospital-based placements and clinical conferences.

name: Pharmacy
overview: The five-year course starts with the basic sciences that underpin pharmaceutical studies, then moves to general and specialised pharmaceutical education in university departments, teaching pharmacies, institutes, laboratories and the pharmaceutical industry. A fast-track route is open to people who already hold a pharmacy BSc, and a combined Pharmacy and Biotechnology pathway is available. Graduates work in public and hospital pharmacies, laboratories, the pharmaceutical industry, research institutes, the international trade in medicines and the management of pharmaceutical materials.

name: Accelerated Pharmacy-Biotechnology Degree Pathway
overview: Pharmacy and biotechnology courses are combined from the start, so two qualifications, a Doctor of Pharmacy and a biotechnologist BSc, are earned in six years rather than eight. The foundation covers physics, general, inorganic, organic and analytical chemistry and biostatistics, followed by cell biology, biochemistry, microbiology, genetics and bioinformatics, and then molecular biology, gene technology, pharmaceutical, medical and environmental biotechnology, quality assurance and data science. Training uses fully equipped student laboratories and research projects. Graduates move into pharmaceutical companies, biotech firms, regulatory agencies, advanced research or doctoral study.

name: Architecture (BSc + MSc)
overview: This is an integrated five-year degree. The first five or six semesters lay groundwork in both the artistic and the engineering sides of architecture: design studios, building construction, materials, structural mechanics, art history, digital architecture, architectural drawing, construction technology and energy systems. Later semesters add ecodesign, urban planning, heritage protection, interior spaces and architectural theory, ending in a complex design project and a thesis. Graduates work in architectural design, town and country planning, heritage preservation, structural design, construction, consulting for authorities and teaching, or continue to doctoral study.

name: Graphic Artist Specialising in Graphic Design
overview: This five-year integrated course, ending in a master's-level qualification, trains artists to work in drawing-based graphic genres. You become familiar with the artistic traditions and outstanding works of contemporary art, and with the means of expression, materials and techniques of graphic art in general. The focus is on the artist's own creative practice in the graphic arts. Graduates have the knowledge needed to continue their studies at doctoral level.

name: Painting
overview: A five-year integrated course leading to a master's in painting, taught in the studio. The early years teach the basic rudiments and techniques of painting, with drawing as the foundation, and the work gradually moves toward independent artistic practice. You develop drawing skills, image-making methods, colour, form and spatial composition, and learn art history and contemporary art, while working in drawing, painting and collage. The aim is a personal way of observing, thinking and representing the world, preparing for a career in art.

name: Sculpture
overview: A five-year integrated course leading to a master's in sculpture, built on studio work and practical skill development. You learn sculptural materials and techniques, professional drawing and modelling, and develop spatial perception, a sense of proportion, and control of colour and shape, grounded in both modern and classical foundations, alongside art history and contemporary art. Graduates are prepared to work as visual artists in professional sculptural practice and to move on to doctoral training.

name: Archaeology
overview: You study archaeology across periods (migration, medieval and early modern, Roman, classical and Byzantine), together with Latin basics, research methods, philosophy, art history, museology and the analysis of find material. Fieldwork is mandatory: excavation practice in the first and fifth semesters, archaeological survey in the fourth and museum education practice in the sixth, in collaboration with outside institutions, and the degree ends with a thesis. Teaching uses lectures, seminars, individual tuition and group projects, and Erasmus exchanges are open. Graduates work as excavation technicians, museum collection managers or in research groups and heritage institutions, or go on to the archaeology master's.

name: Liberal Arts
overview: You choose one major and one minor from Art History, Classical Studies, Film and Visual Studies and Philosophy, plus core courses, so no two students follow exactly the same path. The first year includes academic writing and an introduction to European cultural history, followed by subject courses such as Romanesque and Gothic art, ancient philosophy and film history. Classes are small interactive seminar groups built around discussion and debate, developing critical thinking and written and oral communication. Graduates continue to graduate study or work in museums, libraries, galleries, film studios, media, publishing, education and non-profits.

name: Communication and Media Science
overview: The course covers social communication theory, media studies, cultural anthropology, interpersonal communication and empirical research methods, with practical training in visual communication, photo and video production and multimedia. Specialised topics include the network society, social media and youth cultures, organisational communication, journalism practice, marketing and PR, and the legal and ethical side of communication regulation. A Digital Media and Public Relations specialisation prepares you for journalism and PR work. Graduates work as journalists, editors and content producers, or as communication experts in companies, state bodies and NGOs.

name: English and American Studies
overview: The course combines language development, linguistics and literary analysis with the history and culture of English-speaking countries, including the history of the United Kingdom and the United States and the history of philosophy. Later modules cover British and American literature, contemporary societies and applied linguistics. Teaching is inter- and multi-disciplinary, mixing theory with practice, and you build research techniques and skills in translating non-specialised texts. Graduates are prepared for roles in mass communication, media and tourism and for postgraduate study.

name: International Relations
overview: Core courses include introduction to international relations, diplomacy and negotiation techniques, comparative politics, international and political law, political geography, European integration and EU policies, international economics, globalisation, security and migration policy and twentieth-century world history. Teaching draws on the Faculties of Humanities, Business and Economics, and Law, and mixes theory with practice, including an International Studies in Practice course in semester five. Graduates work in the NGO sector, international organisations, diplomacy, political analysis, journalism and ministries.

name: Pedagogy (Intercultural Educational Assistant)
overview: The course covers learning-centred communication, education systems, comparative education, developmental and educational psychology with practical components, and an intercultural focus: minority education policy in Europe, inclusive education, integration and segregation, and special education cases. Project management, critical thinking and an academic English module support this, and a counselling practical course in the sixth semester gives hands-on experience. Teaching is by lectures, seminars, group work and small research projects. Graduates work as education programme coordinators, international student coordinators, community relations assistants or in refugee education, or continue to teaching at master's level.

name: Pre-school Teaching
overview: The course covers introductory and developmental psychology, pedagogy, and the methods of teaching physical education, mathematics, music and visual education, plus children's literature, games in pre-school, environmental education, cultural diversity in texts, family education and family and children's law. Practice sessions are built in from the first semester and recur in semesters one, three, four and five, mixing traditional and alternative methods with child-centred approaches. Optional modules allow some choice. Graduates are prepared to teach children aged three to seven in pre-school settings.

name: Psychology
overview: The core covers social psychology, cognitive psychology (attention, memory, thinking), evolutionary and developmental psychology and neurology, with supporting subjects in biology, human genetics, psychometrics and personality. Applied areas include health, work and organisational, school and arts psychology. The programme builds skills in experimental science, statistical analysis, research and communication. Graduates can move toward clinical, counselling, educational, forensic, health or occupational psychology.

name: Romology (Roma Studies)
overview: The course trains experts who can communicate Roma community issues to government and non-governmental bodies. You study social studies, the history of the Roma, contemporary Roma art, music and literature, sociolinguistics, ethnography and cultural anthropology, using cooperative learning, group work, fieldwork and research methods. After the first semester you choose a specialisation in Boyash or Romani language and culture, working toward B2 proficiency in that language. Interdisciplinary work with sociologists, teachers, lawyers and doctors prepares graduates for jobs in education, social issues and minority rights.

name: Social Work
overview: You study the theory and practice of social work, social policy, sociology, economics, social law, psychology, public health and education, with an emphasis on critical-reflective thinking, strengths-based approaches and professional ethics rooted in social justice. Coursework includes empirical research methods, human development across the lifespan, family consultation, group and community work, addiction studies, child protection and an introduction to counselling, alongside professional skills training. The entire seventh semester is intensive field practice in a placement chosen according to your interests and institutional availability.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: Mandatory courses cover quantitative methods, microeconomics and macroeconomics, organisational behaviour, corporate finance, accounting, marketing, human resources and international business, with business case studies and operations management in later semesters. Teaching mixes lectures with case studies, practical tasks and teamwork, and guest lecturers from Europe and the United States bring real-world business practice. Optional modules let you deepen a field such as marketing, management or finance. The degree carries EFMD accreditation and prepares you for a business career.

name: Architectural Engineering
overview: You study design studios, architectural drawing, building construction and materials, strength of materials, digital architecture and CAD, architectural history and theory, energy systems, ecodesign, urban planning and professional practice. Teaching combines lectures, workshops and studio work, including perspective drawing, computer graphics and model building, with live projects and case studies, and stresses the architect's responsibility, the detailed development of building systems and teamwork with other design and engineering professionals. The degree ends with a graduation studio, and graduates can continue to a master's within the same faculty.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: The course covers large structures, building engineering, infrastructure such as bridges and highways, and municipal water and wastewater systems. Core modules include materials science, fluid mechanics, structural analysis, reinforced concrete, timber and masonry, steel-composite structures, hydraulics and environmental protection, built on mathematics, natural sciences and economics, with computer and communication skills. Field practice in geodesy and hydrology and diagnostic practicals are part of the study plan, and the final semester is a BSc thesis. Most graduates work in planning, design or management, including construction, structural engineering, transport and urban planning.

name: Computer Science Engineering
overview: Much of the study is laboratory-oriented, and internships let you study and work at the same time. Subjects include programming at several levels, algorithms, electrical engineering foundations, system theory, web and visual programming, operating systems, software technology, information security and project management, moving from fundamentals through intermediate applications to specialisation. The Application Developer specialisation is offered, and the seventh semester is a thesis combined with a capstone programming project. The course suits practice-oriented students and prepares them for IT engineering teams.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The course covers fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, strength of materials, machine elements, structural materials, machining, electrical and control engineering, welding, robotics and flexible manufacturing systems, within a systems view of mechanical, mechatronic and electronic aspects, plus planning and industrial management. Emphasis falls on simulation of engineering systems, numerical modelling, quality control, innovation techniques and polymer and additive technologies. Learning uses laboratory work, projects and field practice at one of the Institute of Mechanical Engineering's industrial partners, and the faculty's international contacts allow study abroad.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: The course prepares electrical and electronic engineers for the design, manufacture and operation of electrical and electronic appliances, equipment and facilities. You build competence in measurement, evaluation, control and management on a base of electrical and electronic engineering theory and its applications. Students are drawn into complex projects and developments already during their university years.

name: Biology
overview: The degree gives a full grounding in biology, with strengths in neurobiology, genetics, microbiology, animal and plant ecology, botany, zoology and plant physiology. The first four semesters cover cell biology, comparative anatomy, plant taxonomy, biochemistry and microbiology. In year two you choose an infra-individual module, with laboratory and cellular biology, or a supra-individual module, with ecology, each mixing lectures, seminars and practicals. Laboratory practices and a botanical and zoological field practice are included, and students can use modern instruments in the Szentagothai Research Centre and join one of its research groups.

name: Biotechnology
overview: The first eighteen months cover general, inorganic, organic, analytical and physical chemistry, physics and biophysics. Later you study biochemistry, microbiology, genetics, molecular biology, genetic manipulation and immunology, with applications in pharmaceutical, medical, food and environmental biotechnology, plus biostatistics and data management. Teaching offers hands-on work with laboratory techniques. Six weeks of practical training in industry or research laboratories fall in semesters five and six, and a written thesis closes the degree. Graduates work in industrial testing, pharmaceutical R&D, production, contract research and bioanalytics, or continue to a master's.

name: Chemistry
overview: The degree gives a full education in chemistry, with directions in inorganic and organic, analytical and environmental, and physical chemistry. Year one builds foundational chemistry and physics, and later courses include chemometrics, theoretical and quantum chemistry, biochemistry, instrumental analysis, advanced organic chemistry, environmental and colloid chemistry and physical chemistry measurements. Teaching combines lectures, seminars with discussion and chemical calculations, and laboratory work with modern instruments, and electives support deeper study in a chosen area.

name: Computer Science
overview: First-year courses cover discrete mathematics, calculus, linear algebra, computer architecture, algorithms, data structures and software technology; later semesters add formal languages, database design, systems design, programming languages and networking. After the fundamentals you choose an Academic track, centred on applied and theoretical mathematics, operations research and algorithm theory, or an Applied track, centred on software development technologies, with room for electives. The final year includes thesis preparation. Graduates work as coders and software developers in the IT sector or continue to a master's.

name: Earth Sciences
overview: The degree gives a general grounding in earth sciences with a strong regional geographical outlook and the option to specialise in geology. Subjects include astronomy, cartography, geomorphology, geophysics, geochemistry, hydrology, meteorology, palaeontology, palaeoclimatology, remote sensing and stratigraphy, plus human geography. Early courses introduce biogeography, meteorology and astronomical geography, the middle semesters move to structural geology and petrographic microscopy, and later ones to engineering geology, geoparks and geotourism and economic geology.

name: Geography
overview: Early semesters cover human geography, planetology and basic natural sciences, then physical geography (geomorphology, climatology, biogeography), human geography (population, settlement, political geography) and regional studies, with a strong GIS basis throughout. Courses usually pair a lecture with a problem-solving seminar. You can concentrate on Environmental Geography, Regional and Urban Development or Tourism Geography. The degree leads on to the university's master's in applied geography, which offers a geomorphology and GIS specialisation.

name: Mathematics
overview: Foundations include logic, computer science, linear algebra, number theory, calculus, geometry, probability, statistics and game theory. Advanced courses cover mathematical programming, operations research, group theory, computer algebra, numerical methods and applied computer science. Most courses pair lectures with problem-solving seminars. The degree is a base for further study in mathematics or computer science, and leads directly to the university's master's in applied mathematics, which stresses operations research, or to master's programmes elsewhere.

name: Physical Training
overview: The course is built from five modules: team and individual sports, medical aspects of sport, social aspects of sport, sport sciences and professional practice. Year one covers psychology, anatomy and sport theory; year two training leadership, physiology, biomechanics and sport psychology; and year three sport management, performance testing, rehabilitation and a thesis. Teaching mixes lectures, seminars, practicals and lab work, with an internship every semester that moves from observing to leading training sessions. You choose a sport such as athletics, handball, basketball, football, swimming or fencing. Graduates work as personal trainers and coaches, or continue to a master's in recreation, coaching or adapted physical education.

name: Physics
overview: After introductory natural sciences and a common core in mathematics, physics and informatics (mechanics, thermodynamics, waves, optics, electricity and magnetism, modern and quantum physics), you specialise in Applied Physics, with advanced experimental and theoretical work, or in Informatics in Physics, covering data acquisition, signal processing in LabView, database management and programming in C#. Teaching includes lectures, laboratories such as CAD and optical measurement, and programming courses in MATLAB and C#, using modern instrumentation.

name: Nursing
overview: The course trains nurses for prevention, treatment, nursing and rehabilitation across health and social care, covering individual, family, community and public health. You study anatomy, pathology and the causes, symptoms, treatment and prevention of illness, and subjects such as basic health care, internal medicine, paediatrics, geriatrics, surgery, obstetrics, community and chronic disease nursing, anaesthesiology, intensive therapy, neurology and psychiatry. Demonstration exercises with lifelike instruments teach blood sampling, infusion therapy and patient examination. Graduates can move to a 1.5-year master's leading to advanced practice roles in intensive, emergency, primary or gerontological care.

name: Midwifery
overview: The four-year course trains midwives to support women through pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period. It is practice-oriented, using modern demonstration devices in teaching and including clinical practice. The qualification is accepted automatically across the European Union, and prior learning can allow some students to complete the degree in a shorter time. The course is run by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

name: Dietetics
overview: You study clinical dietetics for internal medicine, dietetics of infancy and childhood diseases, nutrition management, food chemistry, biochemistry, food technology, practical dietetics, public nutrition, nutrition psychology and nutritional epidemiology, plus the economics of foodservice operations. Specialised clinical areas such as surgical clinical dietetics are included. The course prepares graduates to support patients with weight-related diseases and to manage their diet.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: Physiotherapy is presented as much more than massage or exercise advice, aimed at painless movement. After foundation sciences such as anatomy, you study manual techniques, cardio-respiratory physiotherapy, locomotor diseases, neurological and psychiatric physiotherapy, infant and paediatric care, rehabilitation, electro-diagnostics and radiology. Learning moves from the classroom to skill labs and then to practice in the field with a mentor. Graduates can work in healthcare, wellness centres, fitness facilities, spas and sports clubs, or set up a private practice, and doctoral research and teaching are further options.

name: Classical Instrumental Music Performance (Flute)
overview: Over six semesters you combine lessons on your instrument and performance methodology with orchestral part rehearsal, sight reading, chamber music, choir or orchestra and folk music. Alongside come solfege, music theory, continuo, rhythm practice, Hungarian and world music history, music literature, piano, improvisation, aesthetics and ethics. A diploma concert in the sixth semester concludes the course. Graduates are prepared for orchestras, choirs, chamber ensembles and music institutions, and for master's-level study.

name: Classical Instrumental Music Performance (Guitar)
overview: Practical performance and theory are combined over six semesters: lessons on guitar and performance methodology, chamber music, choir or orchestra, folk music, solfege, music theory, music history, improvisation, piano and continuo, along with concert attendance. The repertoire runs from Renaissance to modern styles, including studies and Bach. A diploma concert in the final semester closes the course. Graduates are prepared to work in orchestras, choirs, chamber ensembles and cultural institutions, or to continue to a master's.

name: Classical Instrumental Music Performance (Piano)
overview: The six semesters blend instrument lessons and performance methodology with chamber music, folk music, concert attendance, continuo, rhythm practice, improvisation, solfege, music theory, music history and orchestral work. Piano repertoire spans Bach preludes and fugues, classical sonatas, virtuoso studies, Romantic pieces and twentieth-century works. A diploma concert is the final performance assessment. Graduates are prepared for orchestras, choirs, chamber ensembles and cultural institutions, and for master's study in music performance.

name: Classical Instrumental Music Performance (Viola)
overview: Six semesters mix individual viola lessons and performance methodology with contemporary-style chamber music, orchestra and choir, orchestral part rehearsal and sight reading, and theoretical study in music theory and harmony, solfege, Hungarian and world music history and folk music. Piano is compulsory for students whose main instrument is not piano, and improvisation, continuo, aesthetics and ethics round out the studies. The repertoire includes Bach suites and solo sonatas and concerto movements. A diploma concert closes the course, preparing graduates for orchestras, chamber ensembles, cultural institutions and master's study.

name: Classical Instrumental Music Performance (Violin)
overview: The course joins practical performance with theory: main-subject lessons in performance methodology, chamber music, orchestral part rehearsal, choir and orchestra, together with music theory, solfege, music history and aesthetics, plus piano, continuo, rhythm practice, sight reading and improvisation. The violin is the specialised instrument, and a diploma concert in the sixth semester is the capstone. Graduates are prepared for orchestras, choirs, chamber ensembles and music institutions, and for master's-level study.

name: Classical Music Singing
overview: The course has a pedagogical orientation, preparing singers for a teaching role as well as for performance. Studies cover voice training, chamber music, choir or orchestra, voice health, solfege, music theory, music history and literature, a foreign language for singers, piano, folk music and repertoire studies with a rehearsal pianist. Pedagogical subjects include professional methodology, the teaching profession, social psychology and ethics. You perform baroque, classical, romantic, twentieth and twenty-first century and folk song repertoire in several languages, and finish with a diploma concert.

name: Orchestral and Choral Conducting
overview: Foundation courses in philosophy, aesthetics, art history, music history and acoustics sit alongside solfege, piano, chamber music, chamber singing and conducting technique and style. Rehearsal work is central, with conducting practice on orchestral scores such as Mozart's Eine kleine Nachtmusik and Schubert's Unfinished Symphony and on choral repertoire, and a final semester with a rehearsal pianist and a diploma choir. Choral conducting is combined with vocal studies. Graduates work in musical institutions, professional ensembles and other occupations that need music education.

name: Electronic Music and Media Art
overview: Theory subjects include philosophy, contemporary aesthetics, art and music history, acoustics, music theory, psychoacoustics and electronic music notation, while the specialised side covers composition practice, sound synthesis and analysis, timbre solfege and MaxMSP programming. Studio practice and computer music projects run through all six semesters, with concert practice, and fine arts and classical music students collaborate in projects that have been running since 1996. Areas include electronic composition, media performance, sound design and network art, with free-chosen topics later on, and the course ends with diploma work.

name: Designer Making: Ceramics Design
overview: Teaching is studio-focused and based in the Zsolnay Cultural Quarter, combining design, material research, 3D design and 3D printing across several materials. Year one brings visual studies, creative design studies and cultural anthropology, then studio ceramics, design methods and design history, followed by art history, industrial product design, 3D modelling, form studies, colour theory and aesthetics. You explore design, craftsmanship, autonomous art and contemporary architecture before specialising, and academic writing and diploma consultations lead to a diploma work in the last semester.

name: Designer Making: Fashion and Textiles Design
overview: The specialism is contemporary tapestry art, taught in a workshop where each student has an individual loom and all materials and tools. Design and workshop work in tapestry and art history run through every semester, alongside the history of textiles, textile colouring, 3D modelling and digital photography; later semesters add sociology, philosophy, scientific writing and professional presentation. You grow from beginner to independent textile artist, with summer internships, university-wide electives and several platforms for showing your work. The final diploma project is an independent body of work, and graduates can continue to a master's.
